Move the green cross of each point until the light lands on the real mark, press Solve and then Apply to the projector. Show a grid picture and look at the wall and the box from the side of the projector.
Measure five spots on the surfaces with the tape and compare them with where the grid lines fall.
manual.measure: the average and the worst error that Solve shows, the error in millimetres at the five checked spots, and photographs of the grid on the wall and the box
manual.criteria: Proposed: the grid lines are straight and continuous on each surface and the checked spots are within the width of a finger. The maintainer sets the real limit after the first runs.

manual.title: Two real projectors with an overlap on one wall
manual.needs: Two projectors, a wall, a PC with two outputs, a camera or a phone with a fixed exposure
steps: Calibrate each projector on its own with at least four measured points, as in M-SPATIAL-1.
Let the pictures overlap by about 15 percent of the wall, set the same overlap under Edge blending on both outputs and show a white picture and then a grid.
Photograph the wall with a fixed exposure and compare the brightness in the overlap with the brightness outside it.
manual.measure: whether the seam can be seen from the usual distance, the brightness of the overlap against the rest in the photograph, and the offset of the grid lines across the seam
manual.criteria: Proposed: the seam is not noticed from the usual distance and the grid lines continue across it with an offset smaller than one line width. The blend values may need a hand adjustment; write down what was needed.

manual.title: Surfaces hiding each other on a real graphics card
manual.needs: A PC with a real graphics card on Windows and one on Linux, and a monitor or projector for the output
steps: Add a wall and a box in front of it, aim the projector so that the box hides part of the wall, and look at the output.
Read the line under the statistics in the 3D mapping block: it must not warn about a missing depth buffer.
Move the box until two surfaces touch along an edge and watch the edge for flicker.
manual.measure: whether the warning appears, whether the box hides the wall as expected, and whether the touching edge flickers
manual.criteria: Proposed: no warning, the hiding is correct, and no flicker where two surfaces meet at an edge. A flicker or a missing depth buffer is added to the known issues.

manual.title: A picture that looks right from one spot
manual.needs: A projector, the corner of a room or a box, a person, a picture with straight lines or a cube
steps: Measure the spot where the person's eyes will be and enter it as the viewer position; choose Picture seen by a viewer.
Calibrate the projector and show the picture.
Look from the viewer spot and from two other spots one step away.
manual.measure: whether lines look straight across the surfaces from the viewer spot, and how far the person can move before it looks wrong
manual.criteria: Proposed: lines look straight and continuous from the viewer spot. How the picture looks from other spots is only written down.

areas.title: Colour management: the colour model, the .cube LUT stage, HDR to SDR for videos, the display of an output, and what depth the real window, master and outputs keep

automated.name: nvj_color_tests
automated.note: the primaries and matrices, the sRGB, gamma, PQ and HLG curves with round trips and published reference points, the two tone mappers, gamut mapping, the HDR to SDR conversion, the display conversion, the .cube parser with damaged and extreme files and the file size limit, trilinear sampling, the sizes of the table in graphics memory, safe file names, and the JSON of settings and output mappings with damaged input and the default staying out of the file; no OpenGL

the real frame buffer, master and float target depth; the picture bit identical with the stage off, switched on and off, without a LUT and at strength 0; identity, inverting, crossing channel and small domain LUTs against the processor model; alpha; memory of the stage planned against measured and freed again; the stage after a deck transition; the HDR shader against the core model for six parameter sets; the two HDR test clips and an SDR clip through the real player on the graphics card and the processor path; and the frame time with and without the stage; the video checks are skipped without FFmpeg (a failure when NYREXVJ_REQUIRE_VIDEO is set); on a virtual screen with software OpenGL

the display conversion of an output in the real output window against the processor model (gamut and curve settings on several colours), its place after the colour correction, the mask, the spatial program, and that the NDI frame of the output carries it; with the fake NDI library

manual.title: Compare the tone mapped HDR picture with a reference player on a real screen
manual.needs: A PC with a real graphics card, an SDR screen that has been checked or calibrated, one or two real PQ files and one real HLG file from a camera or a streaming source, and a reference player that tone maps (for example mpv or a mastering tool)
steps: Open Settings, Performance, Colour and switch on Tone map HDR videos to SDR; keep Convert video colours on the graphics card on.
Play each file in NyrexVJ and in the reference player on the same screen, side by side or one after the other, and try Soft shoulder and Filmic and a reference white of 100, 203 and 300 nits.
Look at skin tones, a bright sky or lamps, a dark scene and saturated colours (a red light, a neon sign) and note where NyrexVJ is darker, brighter or less saturated than the reference.
Switch the option off and note how the same files look, and play an SDR file to check that nothing changes.
manual.measure: for each file and setting: whether highlights keep detail, whether shadows are lifted or crushed, whether colours are clipped or dull, and the settings that came closest to the reference; screenshots of both players
manual.criteria: Proposed: with a suitable reference white the picture is close enough to the reference that a viewer would not call it flat or blown out, and an SDR file looks the same with the option on and off. The maintainer sets the real limit after the first runs.

manual.title: A wide gamut or gamma 2.4 output on a real projector or screen
manual.needs: A projector or screen that can be set to Display P3, Rec. 2020 or a gamma of 2.4, a colorimeter or at least a reference picture on a trusted screen, a PC with an output to it
steps: Put the screen or projector into a known mode (for example Display P3 with gamma 2.2 or a sRGB mode) and open an output window on it.
Show colour bars and a skin tone picture with the default display of the output and note the picture and, if you can, the measured primaries and white.
Set Colour gamut and Transfer of the output to what the screen is really set to and compare again; then set them wrongly on purpose to see what that looks like.
Use Reset display and check that the picture returns to the first one. Check the NDI of that output on a second PC, if there is one.
manual.measure: the measured or judged difference between the default and the matching setting for red, green, blue and white, the colour bars before and after, and what a wrong setting does
manual.criteria: Proposed: with the matching setting the colours of the picture agree with the reference picture and a wrong setting is visibly too dull or too strong. The maintainer sets the real limit after the first runs.

manual.title: A .cube look from a grading program and the cost on a real graphics card
manual.needs: A PC with a real graphics card, a .cube file from DaVinci Resolve or similar with a known look, a short clip or a still, and the same picture graded in the program that made the file
steps: Put the file into the luts folder of the data folder, switch on Colour stage with LUT (experimental), choose it and set strength 1.
Play the clip and compare the picture with the graded picture from the grading program; then try strength 0.5 and a 17, 33 and 65 point table.

Run NyrexVJ --color-selftest tests/data --bench-out color.json on that PC and read the depths and the benchmark, and run a normal show for a few minutes with the stage on while watching the frame time monitor.
Switch the stage off and check that the picture and the frame time return to what they were.
manual.measure: the difference between NyrexVJ and the grading program (by eye and, if possible, by a screenshot comparison), the frame time with and without the stage at the real output size, and the graphics memory shown in the settings
manual.criteria: Proposed: the look is the same as in the grading program and the stage costs well under one millisecond at 1080p on the graphics card; with it off nothing differs. The maintainer sets the real limit after the first runs.

manual.title: What depth a real window gives, on Windows and on Linux, and a 10 bit chain
manual.needs: A PC with a real graphics card on Windows and, if possible, on Linux, a 10 bit capable screen and cable, and the driver setting for 10 bit output or 30 bit colour switched on and off
steps: Run NyrexVJ --color-selftest tests/data and read the first check (depth of the window frame buffer) with the driver setting for 10 bit off and again with it on.
Open Settings, Performance, Colour and read the depth the graphics card reports for the main picture.
Show a long grey ramp on an output and look for banding; if NDI or Spout is used, check what the receiver says about the format.
Run NyrexVJ --output-selftest with and without the fake NDI library on Windows and note any failure.
manual.measure: the reported depth of the window and the master, whether banding is visible, the format a receiver reports, and the result of the selftests on Windows
manual.criteria: Proposed: the reported depth is stated honestly (a 10 bit window is reported as such or as 8 bit, never guessed) and the selftests pass on Windows. This only documents the real state; no 10 bit output is promised.

areas.title: Optical flow: motion estimation, frame interpolation, motion blur and the vector view for video clips, and what they do on real footage, real graphics cards and next to other programs

automated.name: nvj_flow_tests
automated.note: pictures of every frame layout to brightness, the motion estimate on translations, fast motion, static and flat pictures at all three tiers, hard cuts (to black, to a dark copy, between two textured shots), fades and dissolves, pair planning for gaps, order, loops and backwards playback, the governor that lowers the tier, the memory budget and its ceiling, the synthesis against a known 60 frames per second frame, motion blur, the vector picture, moving layers, alpha, frame drops, determinism and the settings keys with damaged values; no OpenGL

the real player with four generated clips (30 and 60 frames per second, a hard cut, a variable frame rate): the feature off creates nothing; 30 to 60 and half speed compared with the real 60 frames per second clip; exact frames bit identical to normal playback; the hard cut equals normal playback; the gap of a variable frame rate and backwards playback fall back with a reason; a full memory budget switches the feature off for the clip; skipped frames; motion blur and the vector view change the picture; a clip with alpha; the cost per step and the state of OpenGL afterwards; needs FFmpeg (skipped without, a failure when NYREXVJ_REQUIRE_VIDEO is set); on a virtual screen with software OpenGL

manual.title: Interpolation and slow motion on real footage on a real graphics card
manual.needs: A PC with a real graphics card, a 1080p output or projector, and real clips: a 24, 25 or 30 frames per second shot with people, one with water or smoke, one with fine particles or a repeating pattern, and one with quick camera movement
steps: Open Settings, Performance, Optical flow and choose Interpolate frames with Balanced.
Play each clip at speed 1 on a 60 Hz output, then at 0.5 and 0.25, and switch the mode Off and On again while watching the same part.
Repeat with Fast and Fine and with Motion blur at shutter 50 and 100 percent, and look at the vector view for each clip.
Watch the video list for state, quality, analysis time and the counters while the clip plays.
manual.measure: for each clip and tier: whether the motion is smoother than with the mode off, where halos, wobble or smearing show (faces, borders, repeating patterns), the analysis time and graphics memory in the list, and whether the picture ever looks worse than the plain picture; screen recordings of both
manual.criteria: Proposed: with Balanced the motion looks smoother than the plain picture on most clips, no clip looks clearly broken, and where the analysis cannot cope the picture falls back to the plain one. The maintainer sets the real limit after the first runs.

manual.title: Variable frame rate, loops, cuts and fades in real files, and the cost at 1080p and 4K
manual.needs: A PC with a real graphics card, a phone video with a variable frame rate, a clip that loops, an edited clip with hard cuts and dissolves, and 1080p and 4K versions of one clip
steps: Play each file in Interpolate mode and look for judder, a picture that jumps back at the loop point, and wrong pictures at the cuts and fades.
Play the 1080p and the 4K clip with Fast, Balanced and Fine and read analysis time, pending and held counts and memory in the video list.
Raise the number of playing videos until the memory limit refuses one, and check the reason in the list.
Run NyrexVJ --flow-selftest tests/data --bench-out flow.json on that PC and keep the file.
manual.measure: the analysis time per pair at 1080p and 4K for each tier, how often pairs were late (pending) or held, whether any cut or loop shows a blended picture, the tier the governor settles on, and the report of the selftest
manual.criteria: Proposed: the picture never shows a blend across a hard cut or the loop point, the governor reaches a tier that keeps pairs on time at 1080p, and the memory refusal is clear. The maintainer sets the real limit after the first runs.

manual.title: Optical flow while VRChat runs on the same PC
manual.needs: A PC that runs VRChat and NyrexVJ together, a normal VRChat world with the headset or desktop mode, one clip for the output
steps: Run VRChat in a busy world and NyrexVJ with a 30 frames per second clip in Interpolate mode on an output, and watch the frame time monitor of NyrexVJ and the frame rate of VRChat for ten minutes.
Do the same with the mode Off and note the difference in both programs.
Repeat with Fast and with Fine and note when the governor lowers the tier or switches the feature off.
manual.measure: frame time and late frames of NyrexVJ and the frame rate of VRChat with the mode off and on at each tier, the tier the governor settles on, and any stutter you can see or hear
manual.criteria: Proposed: with the feature on neither program gets visibly worse than with it off, or the governor lowers the tier or switches the feature off before it does. The maintainer sets the real limit after the first runs.

manual.title: The selftest and the settings page on Windows
manual.needs: A Windows PC with the release build and FFmpeg
steps: Run NyrexVJ --flow-selftest tests/data --bench-out flow.json with NYREXVJ_REQUIRE_VIDEO set to 1 and read the checks.
Open Settings, Performance, Optical flow, switch the modes, tiers, the memory limit and the shutter, play a clip and look at the video list.
Close the program with the mode on, start it again and check that the settings came back.
manual.measure: the result of every selftest check, the numbers in the report (analysis time, frame time, memory) and anything in the settings page that looks wrong
manual.criteria: Proposed: all checks pass on Windows and the settings page works as described. The maintainer sets the real limit after the first runs.

areas.title: Network stream inputs (RTSP, SRT, UDP) and the NDI runtime: real cameras and servers, real networks, Windows, SDI capture cards, the real NDI runtime and VRChat on the same PC

automated.name: nvj_stream_tests
automated.note: the address parser (allowed and refused schemes, characters, hosts, ports, options and ranges), the fields, hiding of passwords and secret options, the plan given to FFmpeg per scheme and profile, the profile table, the limits for codecs and picture sizes, the lag and jitter measures including a clock off by plus and minus 500 ppm over an hour, and the settings keys (default left out, round trip, wrong values and types, an address over 1024 bytes)

automated.name: nvj_ndi_v3_tests
automated.note: the NDI receiver against a stand-in runtime that only has NDIlib_recv_capture_v3, and the version text of a stand-in runtime with and without NDIlib_version, with control characters cleaned

automated.command: LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$FFMPEG_SDK/lib NYREXVJ_REQUIRE_VIDEO=1 python3 scripts/test_stream_input.py --binary build/NyrexVJ --ffmpeg $FFMPEG_SDK/bin/ffmpeg --out stream.json
automated.note: nine default scenarios with real senders on the loopback address: SRT caller and listener and UDP MPEG-TS with MPEG-2, RTSP over TCP with MJPEG from a test server, each through live, signal loss and recovery with the picture checked; a refused codec and a refused picture size; random and damaged data that must not crash the program; one start per profile. Three more scenarios (H.264 over SRT, Low latency, Smooth) run with --scenario srt-h264, srt-low and srt-smooth

automated.name: nvj_picture_convert_tests
automated.note: the shared picture conversion of streams and cameras with 28 widths (also odd ones and ones that are no multiple of 16), 7 heights and 10 pixel formats against a buffer with a marker behind it: nothing may be written further past the end of a picture than half of the padding, and the first pixels must have the right colour. With the padding removed this test reported 307 pictures that wrote up to 28 bytes past the end. The Linux build runs the same test once more under valgrind

manual.title: A real RTSP camera or server, H.264 and H.265
manual.needs: An IP camera or an RTSP server that sends H.264, ideally also H.265, on the same network as the PC, and the release build with FFmpeg
steps: Tick Allow network stream inputs in the Clip window of Stream Input 1 and type the address of the camera, with user name and password if it needs them.
Check that the picture appears, that the password is hidden in the window and in the log, and read size, codec, rate, delay and jitter.
Pull the network cable of the camera for ten seconds, put it back and watch the state and the time until the picture returns.
Repeat with the other profiles and with a second and third camera on Stream Input 2 and 3 at the same time.
manual.measure: the time to the first picture, the frame rate, the delay and jitter shown, the time until the signal is seen lost and until it returns, the processor and graphics memory of the PC with one and with three cameras, and any picture damage
manual.criteria: Proposed: the picture appears, the password stays hidden, the input returns by itself after the cable is put back, and three cameras do not make the show worse than with the feature off. The maintainer sets the real limits after the first runs.

manual.title: SRT and UDP over a real network with loss and jitter
manual.needs: Two PCs on a network (a wired and a Wi-Fi link if possible), an SRT sender such as OBS or ffmpeg, and a way to add loss or delay (a router setting or a tool)
steps: Send an SRT stream to the PC in caller mode and in listener mode and receive it in each profile.
Add packet loss and delay to the link in steps and watch the picture, the jitter value and the catch-ups.
Send UDP MPEG-TS to the PC, with and without loss, and note the result.
Try an SRT stream with a passphrase on both sides and with a wrong one.
manual.measure: for each profile and each loss level: whether the picture stays usable, the jitter value, the number of catch-ups and the behaviour with a wrong passphrase
manual.criteria: Proposed: Smooth rides out the loss that Low latency cannot, a jump to the next key frame leaves no frozen or broken picture, and a wrong passphrase gives a clear message and no picture. The maintainer sets the real limits after the first runs.

manual.title: Windows: the receiver, the settings page and the firewall
manual.needs: A Windows PC with the release build and the Windows FFmpeg libraries, and a sender
steps: Check that the FFmpeg build there has the srt, rtsp and udp protocols; if the page says streams are not available, read the reason.
Run NyrexVJ --fresh --no-update-check --no-welcome --stream-selftest with an address and a sender and read the result.
Open a listener port and check what the Windows firewall asks and what the page shows.
Close the program with a stream running, start it again and check that the settings came back.
manual.measure: whether each protocol opens on Windows, the result of the selftest and the text of the firewall dialog
manual.criteria: Proposed: every protocol that the FFmpeg build contains opens, the page says clearly which one is missing, and the selftest passes. The maintainer sets the real limits after the first runs.

manual.title: The real NDI runtime: version text, receiving and sending
manual.needs: A PC with the NDI Tools or the NDI Runtime installed, a second NDI source and a second NDI receiver (OBS with the NDI plugin, NDI Studio Monitor or another PC)
steps: Open Settings, Output and read the line NDI runtime; note the text and the NDI version that the Tools report.
Receive a source in NDI Input 1, including one with alpha and one that changes its size, and note rate, latency and colours.
Send the NyrexVJ output over NDI and receive it in the other program.
Run NyrexVJ --output-selftest without the fake library and note any failure.
manual.measure: the version text of the runtime, the state, size, rate and latency of each source, whether alpha and size changes work, and whether the NDI output arrives
manual.criteria: Proposed: the version text is shown or the page says none is reported, receiving and sending work as with the stand-in library, and the result is written into this file. No claim about NDI 6 is made until a real runtime of that version was run.

manual.title: An SDI capture card and VRChat on the same PC
manual.needs: A capture card with an SDI input that shows up as a camera, an SDI source, a PC that runs VRChat and NyrexVJ together
steps: Open Camera 1 and check that the card is listed; choose it, note the mode that the card offers and the picture.
Run a stream input (RTSP, SRT or UDP) on Stream Input 1 and the card on Camera 1 together and watch NyrexVJ and VRChat for ten minutes.
Do the same with the feature off and note the difference in both programs.
manual.measure: whether the card is listed and which modes it offers, the picture and its colours, the frame time and late frames of NyrexVJ and the frame rate of VRChat with the stream input on and off
manual.criteria: Proposed: the card works as a camera if its driver supports it, and neither program gets visibly worse with a stream running. No SDI claim is made for any card that was not run.

areas.title: Person detection (mask and 2D tracking from a camera, NDI or stream picture, no model): real cameras, real stage light, a real graphics card, Windows and VRChat on the same PC

automated.name: nvj_person_tests
automated.note: the analysis picture size and the reduction of UYVY and RGBA pictures, blobs, the tracker, an empty scene, detection at all three tiers, sensitivity, alpha edges and softness, temporal stability, several people, people who cross, occlusion, light changes and a strobe, a scene that changes completely, a lost camera, the six signals, the backend interface and its provenance, the governor, wrong input, determinism, the worker thread and its stop, the cost per analysis, and the settings keys with damaged values; no OpenGL

the real engine with computer-made camera pictures: detection off creates nothing and the effect is a pass-through; the empty scene is learned; a person at the top left is found with the right position; the mask lies upright and not mirrored in both modes; a 4:3 camera on a 16:9 output; losing the camera, the signals falling to zero and the person found again; learning the background again; the mask counted in the graphics memory report; the cost per step and the analysis time against the budget; switching off removes everything; the state of OpenGL afterwards; needs no files and no camera; on a virtual screen with software OpenGL

manual.title: A real camera in a real room: who is found, who is not, and how long it takes to learn
manual.needs: A PC with a webcam or capture card and a fixed camera position, a room or stage that can be emptied, two people, a chair and a door or curtain
steps: Open Settings, Performance, Person detection, choose Background difference and the camera, and press Learn background now while nobody is in the picture.
Walk in, stand still, walk out, and watch the mask preview and the People found line.
Carry in a chair and put it down, open the door, and note how long the chair stays a person.
Let two people cross, cover one with the other, and leave and re-enter the picture.
Repeat with Fast, Balanced and Fine, and at sensitivity 25, 50 and 75.
manual.measure: for each case whether the mask matches the person, how often it flickers, how long learning takes, how long a moved object stays in the mask, whether the numbers of two people survive a crossing, and any false person
manual.criteria: Proposed: a person who walks into an empty, steady scene is found within a second and the mask follows the outline well enough for a stage effect; a moved object disappears within about a minute. The maintainer sets the real limit after the first runs.

manual.title: Stage light, projections and exposure: false foreground and repeated learning
manual.needs: A PC with a camera, stage lights or a projector that can change, a fixed camera
steps: Run person detection with the camera on an empty stage and change the lights slowly, in steps, and with a strobe.
Point the camera so that it sees part of the projected show, with and without the person.
Switch the camera's auto exposure and white balance on and off.
Watch the mask preview, the state line and how often it says that the picture changed completely.
manual.measure: the share of the picture that is falsely in the mask for each case, how often learning started again, and what helped (locked exposure, a view without projection, a lower sensitivity)
manual.criteria: Proposed: with locked exposure and a view without projection the mask stays free of false foreground during a normal light change, and the page explains a relearn when it happens. The maintainer sets the real limit after the first runs.

manual.title: Cost on a real graphics card and processor, and VRChat on the same PC
manual.needs: A PC that runs VRChat and NyrexVJ together, a real graphics card, a camera
steps: Run NyrexVJ with person detection on at each tier and at 15 and 30 analyses per second with a Person Key effect on a layer, and watch the frame time monitor and the analysis time on the page for ten minutes.
Do the same with the module off and note the difference in both programs.
Run VRChat in a busy world and note when the governor lowers the tier or the rate or switches the module off.
Run NyrexVJ --person-selftest --bench-out person.json and keep the file.
manual.measure: frame time and late frames of NyrexVJ and the frame rate of VRChat with the module off and on at each setting, the analysis time and p95 on the page, the setting the governor settles on, and the report of the selftest
manual.criteria: Proposed: with the module on neither program gets visibly worse than with it off, or the governor lowers the setting or switches the module off before it does. The maintainer sets the real limit after the first runs.

manual.title: The settings page, NDI and stream sources, and Windows
manual.needs: A Windows PC with the release build, a camera, an NDI source and a stream (or NDI and stream sources from another program)
steps: Run NyrexVJ --person-selftest --bench-out person.json and read the checks.
Switch the module on for a camera, an NDI source and a stream input one after the other, and check the state line, the source choice and the mask preview.
Use the six person sources on a layer opacity, a layer effect parameter and a master slot, and check that a person walking left and right moves the value as expected.
Close the program with the module on, start it again and check that the settings came back.
manual.measure: the result of every selftest check, whether each source type is analysed, whether the sources move the way the person moves, and anything on the settings page that looks wrong
manual.criteria: Proposed: all checks pass on Windows, camera, NDI and stream sources are analysed alike, and the settings page works as described. The maintainer sets the real limit after the first runs.

areas.title: Hardware frame lock and genlock status: the swap group and genlock extension names a real driver lists, what a consumer card, a professional card and a card with a sync board show, the software frame lock next to it, Windows and Linux

automated.name: nvj_hardware_sync_tests
automated.note: the names of software renderers, the vendor from GL_VENDOR and GL_RENDERER, no context gives not checked, a consumer card gives not offered, cards that list names give offered by the driver with the names in a fixed order, a software renderer is never offered, text of any length and with a null character, the same input gives the same result; no OpenGL

the real engine has read the status at start-up, a software renderer is not reported as offering anything, the state agrees with the listed names, and the report carries summary.hardwareFrameLock; run with a clean data directory

the status is read from the driver after the frame lock checks and the software frame lock is still on afterwards; the existing frame lock, delay and sync bar checks run as before; run with a clean data directory
the six new texts of the hardware frame lock line have a translation in all seven tables, with the same printf specifiers

manual.title: What real drivers list: a consumer card, an integrated chip, a professional card
manual.needs: A Windows PC and a Linux PC, and as many of these as can be had: an NVIDIA GeForce, an NVIDIA RTX or Quadro professional card, an AMD Radeon, an AMD Radeon Pro or FirePro, an Intel integrated chip
steps: Start NyrexVJ with --fresh and open Settings, Output.
Read the line Hardware frame lock and the Driver extensions line, and keep a screenshot.
Start NyrexVJ --gpu-diag-selftest --bench-out hardware-sync.json and read summary.hardwareFrameLock in the file.
Repeat with each card and each system, and note the card name and the driver version.
manual.measure: for each card and system: the state shown, the graphics vendor shown, the extension names listed, and whether they match the extension list that a tool such as GPU Caps Viewer, glxinfo or the driver's own information shows
manual.criteria: Proposed: a consumer card and an integrated chip show Not offered, a professional card lists the names its driver documents, and the vendor is right in every case. The maintainer sets the real limit after the first runs.

manual.title: A card with a sync board: what the line says with the board connected, set up and locked
manual.needs: A professional graphics card with a sync board (for example NVIDIA Quadro Sync or AMD FirePro S400), the cables and the driver's tool for frame lock and genlock, optionally a house sync signal
steps: Without the board set up, read the line Hardware frame lock.
Set the board up in the driver's tool until it reports a lock, and read the line again.
Open two output windows with the Frame lock on and the Sync bars test pattern, and film both screens with one camera.
Switch the software Frame lock off and on and film again.
manual.measure: whether the line differs with and without a lock (it is expected not to, because it only reads the extension names), the swap skew shown, the counters of the sync bars on both screens, and whether any of it changes with the driver's lock
manual.criteria: Proposed: the line states what the driver lists and never claims a lock; nothing in the output changes because of the status. The maintainer sets the real limit after the first runs.

manual.title: Two graphics vendors, outputs on another card, and Wayland
manual.needs: A PC with two graphics cards of different vendors or an integrated chip next to a card, and a Linux system that can run Wayland
steps: Open an output window on a display that is connected to the second card and read the line.
Move the main window to the other card and start again.
On Linux, start under X11 and under Wayland and read the line in both.
manual.measure: the state and the names for each case, and whether the line describes the card that really draws the output windows
manual.criteria: Proposed: the state is stated for the main window's card, the page says so, and the Wayland case reads Not offered. The maintainer decides whether the outputs of another card need their own status.

manual.title: The software frame lock next to a driver that lists swap group extensions, and Windows
manual.needs: A Windows PC with a professional card, the release build, two displays or projectors
steps: Run NyrexVJ --output-selftest --bench-out output.json and read the checks.
Run with two output windows for ten minutes with the frame lock on and watch the swap skew and the frame time monitor.
Compare the swap skew and the frame times with the same run on a consumer card.
Check that no setting of the driver changed and that no swap group is reported in the driver's tool.
manual.measure: every check of the self test, the swap skew and frame times with the status Offered and with Not offered, and any difference in the driver's frame lock panel
manual.criteria: Proposed: all checks pass, the frame times do not depend on the status, and the driver's panel shows no change made by NyrexVJ. The maintainer sets the real limit after the first runs.

areas.title: Unreal Engine link: the plugin in a real editor and a packaged game, the connection state, the ping and pong round trip, the Python example client, Windows and Linux

automated.name: nvj_unreal_core_tests
automated.note: the plugin protocol core against the real NyrexVJ sender and parser: decoding, encoding, limits, damaged and cut-off packets, the schema rules, the new pong event; no Unreal Engine

automated.name: nvj_unreal_link_tests
automated.note: the link monitor (waiting, connected, lost after five seconds, ended by bye, reconnect, incompatible schema, rate and longest gap, bad and backwards clock values) and the round trip statistics (minimum, average, maximum, 95th percentile, window of 64, lost, unknown, repeated and late pongs, id wrap around at 16777215), the ping and pong bytes through the real sender and parser; no Unreal Engine

automated.name: nvj_control_tests
automated.note: the ping on the OSC input is accepted for one integer from 0 to 16777215 and refused in every other form, at most 8 are kept per frame, a ping changes no control, the pong is composed, sent over UDP, limited to 8, dropped when the output restarts, and sent in the same update as a hello

the real NyrexVJ with OSC input and output on loopback and the Python example client: three connections (two clean runs with bye, one killed run that is seen as lost after five seconds), hello with schema 1, version and input port, the pongs, the 95th percentile of the round trip below one second, audio and clock data arriving; software OpenGL, so the frame rate and the round trip are those of a software renderer

manual.title: Compile the plugin with a real Unreal Engine, one run per engine version
manual.needs: A Windows PC with Unreal Engine installed (each version to be named as supported, the newest stable release and the one before it are proposed), Visual Studio with the C++ workload for Unreal, and this repository
steps: Copy integrations/unreal/NyrexVJ to <Project>/Plugins/NyrexVJ in a C++ project and generate the project files.
Build the Development Editor target for Win64 and keep the full compiler output.
Build the standalone package with RunUAT.bat BuildPlugin -Plugin=<repo>/integrations/unreal/NyrexVJ/NyrexVJ.uplugin -Package=<out>/NyrexVJ -TargetPlatforms=Win64 and keep the output.
Repeat for each engine version, and note the engine version number, the compiler and the date.
manual.measure: per engine version: whether both builds succeed, the number of errors and warnings, and each error with file and line
manual.criteria: Proposed: a version counts as supported only when both builds finish without errors. The maintainer decides the versions. Every error found here is a bug in the unverified Unreal files.

manual.title: Play In Editor with a running NyrexVJ: connection, data and events
manual.needs: A Windows PC, a project with the plugin from M-UNREAL-1, NyrexVJ with Send OSC data and Receive OSC messages on
steps: Start NyrexVJ with music playing, then press Play In Editor in a level whose Blueprint prints Is Connected, Get Bass and Get Beat Number every second.
Bind On Beat, On Onset, On Connected and On Disconnected to Print String nodes.
Close NyrexVJ and watch the state, then start it again.
Read the log lines starting with LogNyrexVJ.
manual.measure: whether the values move with the music, whether each event fires once per occurrence, the time until Connected after NyrexVJ starts, the state after NyrexVJ closes cleanly and after it is killed with the task manager
manual.criteria: Proposed: Connected within 3 seconds of NyrexVJ's first hello, Ended after a clean close, Lost after about 5 seconds without a bye, no event twice, no error line in the log.

manual.title: A packaged game with the plugin
manual.needs: A Windows PC with Unreal Engine and the project from M-UNREAL-2
steps: Package the project for Windows (Development), start the packaged game and NyrexVJ.
Repeat the checks of M-UNREAL-2 in the packaged game.
Start the packaged game first and NyrexVJ second, then the other way round.
manual.measure: whether the plugin is in the package, whether the checks of M-UNREAL-2 give the same result, and the log of the packaged game
manual.criteria: Proposed: identical behaviour to the editor, in both start orders.

manual.title: The round trip in a real project, and in comparison with the Python client
manual.needs: A Windows PC with a graphics card, Unreal Engine, NyrexVJ at its normal frame rate, and for the second part a second computer on the same network
steps: Show Get Link Status in the level (average, 95th percentile, pings lost) while NyrexVJ renders a heavy look at 60 frames per second.
Run integrations/unreal/examples/nyrex_monitor.py on the same PC at the same time on the same ports (stop the game first, the port can be held only once) and compare.
Repeat with NyrexVJ on the second computer, sending to the PC's address.
manual.measure: the average and the 95th percentile of the round trip in the game, the Python client and over the network, and the number of lost pings in 10 minutes
manual.criteria: Proposed: on one PC the round trip stays below two NyrexVJ frame times and no ping is lost. The maintainer sets the limits after the first runs.

manual.title: Failure and recovery
manual.needs: A Windows PC with the project from M-UNREAL-2, a second program that can hold a UDP port, and a firewall that can be switched on
steps: Hold the listen port (9011) with another program, start the game, then free the port.
Block UDP 9011 in the firewall for a minute while NyrexVJ sends, then allow it again.
Switch Measure Latency off and check that no ping reaches NyrexVJ.
Send controls (Set Master Level, Trigger Column) from the plugin and watch NyrexVJ.
manual.measure: the log line about the busy port (once, not repeatedly), the time until the plugin connects after the port is free, the states during the firewall block, and whether the controls arrive
manual.criteria: Proposed: one log line, connected within the retry time plus 2 seconds, Lost during the block and Connected again after it, controls arrive.

areas.title: ResoPort (Resolume import), translucent 3D meshes, output while the window is minimized or moved, the 15 transitions and the glass effects: real Resolume compositions, real Windows, real graphics cards

automated.name: nvj_resoport_tests
automated.note: the XML reader (entities, comments, CDATA, a document type declaration with definitions, limits), a Resolume composition read into a document, a cut and a randomly changed file (3,000 rounds), the blend names, the media finder (next to the file, recorded path, extra folder, only media file names) and the build of a composition with its report
the real engine draws every one of the 15 transition types (it must run, start on the old clip and end on the new clip); it does not measure the look of the middle of a transition
the 3D scene player, including the model with one solid mesh in blend mode (the branches must not show through each other)

the whole ResoPort import in the real window (open, check a file, report, import, the composition and the library afterwards) and that the engine keeps counting frames while the interface is not drawn; on a virtual screen with software OpenGL, so it proves the logic and not how a real minimized window behaves

every clip, effect and transition shader compiles, including Prism Glass and Frosted Glass; it says nothing about how they look. Use an empty data folder: media left in a data folder show up as video clips that this check counts as failures

manual.title: A real Resolume show composition
manual.needs: A composition saved by Resolume Arena or Avenue (a show you really use) with its media, and this build
steps: Open File, Resolume import (ResoPort)... and give the .avc file; press Check file and read the report against the composition in Resolume (clips, layers, decks).
Press Import and play a few cells of every layer.
Note every clip, layer setting or name that Resolume has and NyrexVJ does not show.
manual.measure: clips counted in the report against clips in Resolume, cells that are empty or in the wrong place, layers whose blend mode or opacity differs, the tempo, and the time the check and the import took
manual.criteria: Proposed: every media clip lands at the same layer and column, nothing is reported as imported that is not, and everything that is skipped is named in the report.

manual.title: Resolume blend names and the tempo in a real file
manual.needs: Resolume with a composition of four layers, each with another blend mode (Add, Multiply, Screen, Overlay, Soft Light, Difference and others in turn), a tempo of 133 BPM, saved as .avc
steps: Save the composition from Resolume and import it with ResoPort.
Read the line with the blend modes that are not known and look at the layer panel after the import.
Repeat with other blend modes until every mode of Resolume that you use has been seen.
manual.measure: the names Resolume writes for each blend mode, which of them ResoPort maps and which it lists as unknown, and whether the tempo is taken over
manual.criteria: Proposed: a blend mode that has a counterpart is mapped, one that has none is listed by name, and the tempo of the composition is the tempo after the import.

manual.title: DXV media in an imported composition
manual.needs: A Resolume composition whose clips are DXV movies, FFmpeg for the conversion, this build
steps: Import the composition with ResoPort and watch the conversion that the library starts.
Play the converted cells next to the original in Resolume.
manual.measure: whether the DXV files are found and copied, whether the HAP copies are made and used, and whether picture and speed match Resolume
manual.criteria: Proposed: the movies play after the conversion at the right speed and the cells hold the converted clips.

manual.title: Output while the window is minimized, moved or a menu is open (Windows)
manual.needs: A Windows PC with a second display or OBS taking the Spout output, a playing clip with motion and this build
steps: Start NyrexVJ with an output window on the second display (or Spout into OBS) and play a clip.
Minimize the main window and watch the output for a minute.
Restore it, then drag the main window by its title bar for ten seconds, drag its edge to change the size for ten seconds, and keep a menu open for ten seconds.
manual.measure: whether the output keeps moving in each case, any frozen stretch in seconds and the frame counter of OBS or the output
manual.criteria: Proposed: the output never freezes for more than a fraction of a second in any of the four cases, and the interface is drawn again after the restore.

areas.title: Audio analysis 2: the optional beat tracker (tempo, phase, confidence, grid beats), the audio latency setting, the adjustable band split and the left, right or mixed channel choice

automated.name: nvj_audio_tracker_tests
automated.note: synthetic tracks at 100, 128 and 150 BPM, a tempo change from 120 to 140, a 10 s cross-fade between 124 and 128 BPM, silence and its return, a quiet break, clipping, hats on the off-beats, sixteenth hats, three frame rates, the latency setting in both directions, the channel picking, the band split, the classic path unchanged by the switch, and the CPU time per frame

automated.name: nvj_audio_tests
automated.note: the existing analysis: bands, smoothing, the demo signal at three tempi and the classic beat detection that the new tracker sits next to

manual.title: The beat tracker with real music and a real audio input
manual.needs: A PC with a real audio input or system audio, music with a clear kick at a steady tempo, a DJ mix with a tempo change, a second track without a steady beat (ambient or a live band), and a stereo source with a different signal on each side
steps: Open Settings, Audio, set Beat tracking to Improved, play a house or techno track and watch the tempo, the Tempo and Beat percentages and Locked; note the time until Locked and the tempo you see against the tempo you know.
Play a DJ mix through a tempo change and a break and watch whether the tempo follows and whether the beats keep going through the break; then stop the sound for ten seconds and start it again.
Play the ambient track and check that the tracker does not lock on noise and that the picture falls back to the classic detection when it is not locked.

Route a click track to a loopback or a second input, show the beat in the output next to the click on a recording or a scope, and set Audio latency until both agree; write down the value and the audio device.

Send a different signal to the left and the right channel and switch Channel between Mix, Left and Right; check that the Audio window shows the chosen side only and that the capture restarts without a crash.

Move the two split sliders while a track with a loud bass line plays and check that the Bass, Mid and High meters follow; set Beat tracking back to Classic and check that the show behaves as in the version before.
Run a show of 30 minutes with Improved on while the video plays and look at the frame time and the CPU use of the audio thread.
manual.measure: the time until Locked, the tempo error against the known tempo, whether the grid beats fall on the kicks (a recording or a scope), the latency value that matches on your interface, the CPU use with Classic and with Improved, the frame time, and anything that jumps or stays wrong
manual.criteria: Proposed: Locked within 5 s on steady music, the tempo within 1 BPM, grid beats within 40 ms of the kicks after the latency setting, no lock on the ambient track, no crash when the channel changes, and no measurable change of the frame time between Classic and Improved.

areas.title: Transition designer: deck transitions of your own as GLSL or ISF files (outgoing and incoming picture, progress, controls, preview, fallback to the built-in transition)

automated.name: nvj_transition_tests
automated.note: the transition pragma and its limits, ISF transitions, the example files, the file scan (new, changed, broken, gone, over the limit), the preset round trip of the name and the values, and hostile names

automated.name: nvj_isf_tests
automated.note: the ISF cases that must still be refused (one picture only, an input image next to the pictures, a pass with a target)

renders custom transitions through a real OpenGL context: start and end on the right deck, a hard wipe in the middle, the progress value, a control with its default and a stored value, a switch while a transition runs, six quick switches, a change to a built-in transition, a compile error, a deleted file, an unknown name, a repaired file, a deck with alpha, a transition that writes alpha 0, a deck with feedback buffers, the preview at three progress values, and the built-in transitions next to them
adds the frame time of no transition, two built-in transitions and three custom ones (one with sixteen taps)

automated.name: nvj_compat_tests
automated.note: the frozen settings and preset fixtures are still written byte for byte as before when no transition file is chosen

manual.title: Custom transitions on a real graphics card, a real output and a real show
manual.needs: A PC with a graphics card, an output window or Spout or NDI to OBS, two decks with different clips (one with feedback effects and one with a layer that has alpha), and the example files from docs/shaders
steps: Copy transition_iris.glsl and isf_transition_slide.fs into the shaders folder, open the Trigger window and check that both are listed under Your transitions, that the sliders show and that the preview moves with the progress slider.

Choose each of them, switch between the two decks with beat sync on and off and with several lengths, and compare the picture in the output (and in OBS) with the preview and with a built-in transition of the same length.
Switch decks again in the middle of a custom transition, switch back and forth quickly, change the transition type during a run, and look for jumps, flashes or a black frame.
Edit the file in the shader editor while a transition runs, save a version that does not compile, then repair it, and check that the show never stops and that the red message appears and goes away.
Delete the file while the deck uses it and switch decks; check that the built-in transition next to it runs; then put the file back and check that it is used again.
Use a sixteen-tap shader and a transition on two decks with video and effects at the output size you play at and look at the frame time and the graphics memory during the transition and after it.

Save a preset and the session with a custom transition and sliders moved, restart, and check name and values; load the same preset on a PC that does not have the file and check that the built-in transition runs and nothing is lost.
manual.measure: the frame time and graphics time during a custom transition against a built-in one of the same length, the graphics memory, any visible jump or black frame, the compile time of a file the first time it is used, and the behaviour of the output (Spout, NDI, recording) during a transition
manual.criteria: Proposed: no visible jump or black frame at the start or end, the frame time during a custom transition within 10 percent of a built-in one with the same number of taps, a broken file never stops the output, and the choice survives a restart.

areas.title: GPU feedback lab: a memory budget for feedback buffers, buffer reuse, freeze and reset, the frame time as uDelta, and the new effects Time Echo, Motion Smear, Feedback Transform and Accumulate

automated.name: nvj_feedback_tests
automated.note: the settings keys and their limits, the two control targets and what they call, the four new effects (order, four controls, defaults, feedback flag, novelty entry), the unchanged source of Trails and Hue Feedback, the budget arithmetic, and a node graph with feedback, a chain that fills the 96 node limit and a graph forced into a loop

renders the feedback effects through a real OpenGL context: the half-life of Time Echo at 30, 60 and 120 frames per second and across a pause, the 8 bit residue of Trails next to a Time Echo that reaches black, Freeze, Reset, the three modes of Accumulate, Motion Smear and Feedback Transform, the direction of the echo, the budget (four buffers, smaller buffers, a refused buffer), eight resolution changes, the layer resolution, reuse on and off, the pool, deck switches, and a 1200 frame run with random changes of resolution, deck, quality, budget, freeze, reset and effect
adds the frame time, the first frame and the feedback memory of no effect, Trails, the four new effects, a frozen Time Echo and four layers with and without Time Echo
compiles the four new effects on the driver in use

automated.name: nvj_compat_tests
automated.note: the frozen settings and preset fixtures are still written byte for byte as before (the two new settings keys are written only when they are not the default)
every new text has a translation in all seven tables, with the same printf specifiers

manual.title: Feedback effects, the memory budget, freeze and reset on a real graphics card in a real show
manual.needs: A PC with a graphics card, an output window or Spout or NDI to OBS, a song or a live input, and optionally a MIDI controller and a second PC on the network sync
steps: Put Time Echo, Motion Smear, Feedback Transform and Accumulate on four layers over moving clips, play with the four controls and check that the half-life sliders feel the same at 30, 60 and 144 frames per second (switch the frame rate limit).

Open Settings, Performance, Feedback, set the budget to 64 MB at 4K output, and check that the buffers shrink without a jump, the message says how many run smaller, and the show keeps playing; then raise it and check that they return to full size.
Set the budget so small that a buffer is refused and check that the effect shows the live picture without trails, the orange message appears, and nothing crashes or flashes.

Map Freeze feedback and Reset feedback to MIDI notes and OSC, hit them during a drop, and check that the trails hold while frozen, that Reset clears them in one frame, and that Freeze is off after a restart.
Switch decks quickly for ten minutes with feedback on both, change the resolution twice, and watch the graphics memory in Settings, Performance for growth.
Run the show for an hour with a changing mix of feedback effects and compare the graphics memory at the start and at the end.
On two PCs with the network sync, update both to 0.66.0, trigger Freeze and Reset on the master, and check that both follow.
manual.measure: the frame time with and without feedback effects at the output size you play at, the graphics memory of the feedback buffers (Settings, Performance, Memory) at the start and after an hour, the time of the first frame after an effect starts, and any visible jump when a buffer changes size
manual.criteria: Proposed: the half-life within 10 percent of the slider value at 30, 60 and 144 frames per second, no visible jump or black frame when a buffer shrinks or grows, a refused buffer never stops the output, the feedback memory after an hour within 5 percent of the start, and Freeze and Reset through MIDI and OSC working in the same frame.

areas.title: GPU effect graph optimizer: the last layer is drawn straight into the output, the colour look needs no extra picture, and a transition draws its two decks without a copy, with the switch Skip passes that only copy

automated.name: nvj_graph_tests
automated.note: the setting and its tolerance (default on, written only when off), when the last pass is neutral (grade, level, Blackout, hold), when a chain is empty, the route table for the optimizer on and off with and without a colour stage, the layer swap parity from 0 to 64 swaps, and the counters

renders every route through a real OpenGL context twice, with the optimizer off and on, in the same frame, and compares every pixel: one to four layers, all 14 blend modes, five blend orders, a hidden layer, bypass, solo, six colour grades, three levels, Blackout, hold, master and layer effects, reduced layer resolution, three output sizes, the colour look (direct, half strength, graded, dimmed, with a master effect, even and odd swaps), fade, Radial, Glitch and custom transitions (graded, with an effect, with a colour look), four feedback sequences of 20 frames each (Trails on a layer and on the master, a hidden feedback layer with a swapping blend, three layers with two feedback), switching the optimizer in the middle of a transition, and the counters; the alpha of the picture stays 255

adds the frame time (average, median, 95th and 99th percentile, worst), the graphics memory and the skipped passes per frame of one layer, four layers, four layers with a colour look, four layers with a master effect and a transition, each with the optimizer off and on in four alternating rounds, and the number of different pixels
the memory the colour look reports: only the look itself with the optimizer on, the look and a picture of the output size with it off
the five new texts of the Render graph section have a translation in all seven tables, with the same printf specifiers

manual.title: Skip passes that only copy on a real graphics card in a real show, with and without a colour look and during transitions
manual.needs: A PC with a graphics card, an output window or Spout or NDI to OBS, a show with four layers of video and effects, a LUT file, and optionally a second PC on the network sync
steps: Play a show with four layers, no master effect and a full level, open Settings, Performance, Render graph and note the frame time and the counter. Turn Skip passes that only copy off and on and compare the frame time at the output size you play at.
Look at the output while switching the setting off and on during a bright, busy scene and check that no frame changes, flashes or goes dark.
Switch on a colour look (LUT) and check the frame time and the Extra graphics memory in Settings, Colour with the setting on and off; the memory must be lower with it on and the picture the same.
Run a fade, a wipe and a custom transition between two decks, switch the setting in the middle of one, and check the picture does not jump.
Add a master effect and a level below full and check that the picture is still right and the counter stops counting while they are on.
Play for an hour with the setting on and compare the graphics memory at the start and at the end.
Repeat the first step at 4K output and on a second PC with the network sync, if you have them.
manual.measure: the frame time with the setting off and on at the output size you play at, the graphics memory with a colour look on and off, and the passes and copies skipped in the counter
manual.criteria: Proposed: the picture with the setting on is the same as with it off in every case you try, no flash or jump when the setting is switched, the frame time with it on is not above the frame time with it off, the graphics memory with a colour look is lower with it on, and the memory after an hour is within 5 percent of the start.
